description: TechTechTech!! Come and join us to solve a big problem - Farm Optimization!!!  Lot's of fun!!!
summary:
FarmSmart is a decision making tool that helps farmers optimize their whole farm, one field at a time. Most farmers manage many fields, each with different soil, water, terrain and crop history, but planting decisions are usually made for the farm as a whole. FarmSmart lets a farmer add each field by finding it on a 3D globe or drawing its boundary. For each field, FarmSmart gathers NASA Earth observation data for that exact spot: weather history, soil moisture, water storage, evapotranspiration, satellite greenness (NDVI) and terrain, along with USDA soil, cropland and county yield data. It tests 16 crops and rotation options against 26 years of real weather, including drought years. Farmers can then weigh their fields as a portfolio and decide which crop goes where to maximize expected profit and minimize risk across the whole operation.

This matters because good field level data rarely reaches farmers in a usable form. FarmSmart turns scattered satellite datasets into clear choices, showing each value with its source and date. Balancing crops across fields spreads weather and market risk, protects soil and saves water.  Tool works US, globally in both browser and mobile phone.
details:
What it does
FarmSmart is a decision making tool for a whole farm, built one field at a time. A typical farm is a portfolio of fields that differ in soil, drainage, slope, water access and recent crops, and the planting plan for one field affects risk and profit for all of them. FarmSmart helps a farmer decide which crop to plant in each field so the farm as a whole earns more and carries less risk.
This is a working tool. Data is live. All NASA data links have been integrated.
For easy of understanding a Demo section has been included where one can: 1) have guided tour, 2) view a sample case of a whole farm with 3 fields, 3) Try 8 different sample farms. We encourage you to try and build your own whole farm portfolio!!!

How it works

  1. Add fields one at a time. The farmer finds each field by place, address or coordinates, then confirms or draws its boundary on a 3D globe or 2D editor. They add their own crop history and field details.
  2. Build an evidence profile for each field. A backend service pulls live data for that location and keeps each value’s resolution, date, units and quality flags. Sources include NASA POWER weather history, HLS Landsat/Sentinel-2 30 m NDVI with cloud and shadow masks, SMAP soil moisture, GRACE/GRACE-FO water storage, ECOSTRESS evapotranspiration, SRTM terrain, USDA Cropland Data Layer, SSURGO/STATSGO2 soils, NASS county yields, USGS streamflow and elevation, ERA5, PRISM, SoilGrids, NLCD, LANDFIRE and FAO GAEZ.
  3. Test options against past seasons. Each field’s candidate crops and rotations, chosen from 16 crops, are replayed against 26 years of real weather, including drought years. This shows how each option would have performed in good and bad seasons.
  4. Optimize the portfolio. The farmer compares results across all fields and chooses a crop for each one, balancing expected profit against risk. One field might be best for corn, while a droughty field might be safer in a more tolerant crop. Spreading crops across fields reduces the chance that one bad season hurts the whole farm.
  5. Act and review. FarmSmart produces ranked explanations, an action plan with weather-rule alerts, and saved reports the farmer can export.

Benefits and intended impact
Farmers make high-stakes planting decisions once a year, usually with little field-specific data. FarmSmart brings NASA science down to the scale of each field and then back up to the farm as a whole. The goal is higher, steadier farm income, less exposure to drought and weather risk, and rotations that protect soil and water over time.

Tools and technologies
FarmSmart is a Node.js web app with a JavaScript client, a CesiumJS 3D globe, a 2D boundary editor and a database for saved fields, plans and alerts. Data comes through NASA Earthdata (CMR, OPeNDAP, LP DAAC, PO.DAAC and NSIDC), the NASA POWER API, USDA Soil Data Access, NASS Quick Stats, USGS Water Data APIs, Open-Meteo/ERA5 and RCC ACIS (PRISM). It has 173 automated tests covering units, missing and fill values, quality masks, dates and coordinates, and credential safety, plus browser checks on desktop and mobile. As this is built in 2 days there may be some bugs in the github to website connection. Otherwise when test fields loaded successfully unless we noted otherwise.

How it’s creative
Most agricultural data tools show maps of one place. FarmSmart treats the farm as a portfolio and treats NASA data as evidence for a business decision. It replays real past seasons on each of the farmer’s fields, then helps the farmer decide where to plant what. Every number shows its source, date and resolution, so the farmer knows how much to trust it. It also has tools for Email notifications, can test over any year such as 2012 and offers a glimpse of the future using twin fields. Machine learning is used in key areas. Radial buttons are used to hover over to obtain key information. Where applicable we have added in additional languages such as Spanish. Adding in revenue and costs we think gives an immediate benefit to the farmer to start using the tool. Historical tracking of fields as well as neighboring fields gives lots of insight.

Factors we considered

  • Scientific honesty: profit, yield and risk outputs are planning estimates, not calibrated forecasts, and are labeled that way. Our trained weather models did not beat a simple historical-average baseline, so we use the baseline and say so.
  • Missing data: the app shows when data is missing and never fills gaps with made-up values.
  • Farmer control: outside data never silently overwrites the farmer’s own inputs.
  • Security: API credentials stay on the server.
  • Data terms: each source is attributed according to its license.
  • Usability: it works on mobile, and a 28-second guided walkthrough introduces the app.

Our Team
The team was lead by a Grade 9 student who has been coding since he was in Grade 1. He is keen to use technology for helping others. Currently he has a portfolio of home made wind turbine, autonomous rover and working on a humanoid. He has been helped on this project by his keen Grade 4 brother. So many fun things to build!!

Note: Since we are minors we were not able to show our faces in the video. Our computer system is a bit old and laggy so the video quality and sound is not the greatest.

My brother and I highly appreciate the encouragement and support from our parents especially in letting us grind this out with little sleep.

Live app: https://farmsmart-odo9.onrender.com
Code: https://github.com/FarmSmartPilot/farmsmart

Use of AI tools
FarmSmart was developed with AI coding assistants, mainly OpenAI Codex and also Anthropic’s Claude. We used them to write and refactor code, integrate data sources, write tests and draft documentation. All data comes from the cited public sources, not from AI. No NASA logos or branding were generated.
